scenes.headline: How Nanbeige4.3-33B is built as a teacher
scenes.sub: A plain dense model whose real cost is its cache.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Painter! Nanbeige four point three is a thirty-three billion parameter model, released first so it can teach smaller ones. Let's open it up.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Build the strongest agent you can afford first, then use it as the teacher for small models. The teacher is released now; the student is not.
scenes.say: Build the strongest agent you can first, then use it to teach small models. The teacher is out now. The student is not.

steps.say: A token goes up through fifty-two identical blocks. No experts, no loops, no sliding windows.
The feed-forward layer holds about four fifths of every block's weights.
Seven query heads share each key and value head, so only eight heads are cached.

scenes.title: Cache per token, f16
scenes.note: every layer caches; Qwen's hybrid caches only 16
scenes.say: But every layer keeps a cache. That is two hundred eight kilobytes a token, over three times Qwen's hybrid. At long context the cache, not the weights, is the bill.

scenes.title: How a tool call is written

items.text: Results return as a user turn

scenes.say: The chat template shows how it acts. It thinks first, then names a function in XML. Results come back as a user turn.

steps.say: A base model goes through post-training. The recipe, the data and the environments are not published.
Out comes the thirty-three billion teacher, with open weights.
It is then meant to teach a three billion student. How, the team has not said.

scenes.label: benchmarks the card lists, leading Qwen3.8-27B, Muse-Glimmer and Gemma4-31B
scenes.say: The card reports it leading on seventeen of twenty benchmarks against three rivals. Those are the publisher's own runs.

scenes.text: A teacher is a claim about the future; the cache is a bill you pay today.
scenes.mark: the cache is a bill you pay today
scenes.say: A teacher is a claim about the future. The cache is a bill you pay today.
To recap: a plain dense model, a heavy cache, and a teacher whose student has not arrived.
